newsitem.title: UK: Bunzl confident of future prospects. [CORRECTED 07:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bunzl confident of future prospects. [CORRECTED 07:54 GMT]

text.p: Paper and plastics group Bunzl Plc said on Monday it was confident of its future prospects, despite an uncertain outlook for pulp and paper prices.

"We believe our strong positions in resilient markets and our proven success in acquiring and integrating businesses will enable us to continue to move the group forward with confidence," Bunzl said in a statement.

The group announced interim pre-tax profits of 55.8 million stg, a 12 percent improvement on the same period in 1995 when it reported a pre-tax figure of 50.0 million stg (corrects from 55.0 million stg).
The interim dividend was raised to 2.2 pence per share from 2.0 pence for the same period the previous year. Earnings per share were up nine percent at 8.1 pence compared with 7.4 pence.
Bunzl said sales had risen by only one percent, to 887.5 million stg from 879.5 million stg, but added this was in spite of deflationary pressures in most parts of its business.
Chairman Anthony Habgood said he was pleased to announce "another very satisfactory set of results" against a background of extremely volatile prices in both paper and plastics.

"The outlook for prices is uncertain although, at least in the very short term, rises generally appear somewhat more likely than further reductions, even if, in some cases, from very low levels," Habgood said.
A positive contribution from recent acquisitions and new U.S. business coming on stream, Habgood said he expected continued satisfactory progress for the group.
